# Introduction

The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB) commissioned PolicyEngine
to estimate the effects of fifteen reforms to the taxation of Social Security
benefits over `2026`-`2100`. They comprise `option1` through `option12` except
`option6`, a reverse-Roth proposal, a `93%` benefit-taxation benchmark, full
MAGI inclusion of benefits, and the 2005 Tax Panel simple deduction. We also
report `option6`, a shorter phase-in variant of the phased Roth swap, as a
sensitivity case. We simulate every reform on the full populace microdata at a
set of anchor years, interpolate between them, and publish the annual results,
trust-fund splits, and household impacts on an
[interactive dashboard](https://policyengine.org/us/taxation-of-benefits-reforms).

## Current-law baseline

Under current law, beneficiaries pay income tax on part of their Social Security
benefits once their combined income exceeds statutory thresholds. They include
up to 50 percent of benefits in taxable income above the first threshold and up
to 85 percent above the second [@irs2024pub915]. The Treasury credits that
revenue to the Social Security Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance
(OASDI) trust funds and the Medicare Hospital Insurance (HI) trust fund
[@ssa2026trustees; @medicare2026trustees].

We score every reform against current law under the 2026 Trustees Reports'
intermediate assumptions. The Trustees built the 2025 reconciliation act (the
One Big Beautiful Bill Act) into those assumptions, including the temporary
bonus senior deduction and its scheduled expiration after `2028`
[@jct2025bonus]. PolicyEngine models the same law, so our simulations and our
calibration targets describe one current law. Several reforms extend, repeal,
or replace the bonus senior deduction, so its scheduled expiration shapes their
effects.

## Research questions

We ask two questions:

1. How do alternative Social Security benefit-taxation reforms alter trust-fund
   revenue, household tax burdens, and long-run fiscal outcomes?
2. What data and validation does a `2026`-`2100` microsimulation need to
   produce interpretable estimates?
